summary: A 100-foot Aermotor lookout the Forest Service erected in 1931 on the Olustee battlefield site; a CCC marker makes the origin contested.

access.note: On national forest land beside the battlefield trail. Current climbing rules were not confirmed; check before you climb.

visit.trail_note: A 2.3-mile hike through the state park passes the tower, according to a trail listing. We did not confirm current climbing rules.

events.note: Erected by the U.S. Forest Service, per the register and the Eastern US Lookouts page
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 1, 2013

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Eastern US Lookouts page date the tower to 1931 and credit the Forest Service. The HMDB marker calls the tower a CCC project and dates the corps from 1933, so the marker may refer to later CCC work at the site; no source we read describes such work. Unresolved.

notes_for_editor: The 1931 build date and Forest Service credit come from the NHLR page and the Eastern US Lookouts page, which agree. The HMDB marker's CCC claim conflicts with that date and is unresolved; the story says so. Current climbing access is not confirmed by any official source. The only climbing statement is in a Komoot trail listing, a third-party app whose text may be generated, so verify with Osceola National Forest or Florida State Parks before publishing the access level as public (floridastateparks.org returned HTTP 403). The marker's listed coordinates are within roughly 15 m of the register's, so the marker sits at the tower. The record's height_m of 30.5 agrees with the register's 100 ft, but the register does not say whether that is to the cab floor, so it is not restated as a fact. A USFS page on the Olustee Experimental Forest timed out and was not read.
